result: I would make it so that every person, at some point in their life, experiences a moment of genuine, unforced understanding of someone they had previously seen as an enemy or a stranger—not through argument or instruction, but through the quiet, involuntary recognition of shared fear, shared hope, or shared grief. Not to erase difference or conflict, but to make the *possibility* of that recognition universally available, so that cruelty and indifference would always carry a faint, inescapable echo of the question: "What if I had listened?"
